blocks.content: Quiz: How does the Rabin-Karp algorithm minimize redundant comparisons in string-matching?
Tap an option below to answer:
By comparing each letter of the text and the pattern.
In the Rabin-Karp approach, string comparison is done only if they have equal hash values, not letter by letter.
In the Rabin-Karp approach, string comparison is done only if they have equal hash values, not letter by letter.
By comparing hash values of the pattern and text's substring before a direct comparison.
In the Rabin-Karp approach, we compare the pattern with the subtext only if they have equal hash values.
In the Rabin-Karp approach, we compare the pattern with the subtext only if they have equal hash values.
By finding the length of the pattern and the text.
Finding the length of the pattern and the text doesn't directly minimize redundant comparisons.
Finding the length of the pattern and the text doesn't directly minimize redundant comparisons.
By sorting the text and pattern alphabetically prior to comparison.
Alphabetically sorting the text and pattern prior to comparison does not represent the Rabin-Karp algorithm.
